I tried them based on that and the site crashed (503!) when I had symbols in my password! This wouldn't surprise me, given their engineering abilities, and I'd be terrified to leave anything critical in their hands.
I did briefly use Porkbun and have to say that the minimalist UI that actually loads fast was a breath of fresh air and was so much less frustrating than Namecheap.

Porkbun is cheaper than Namecheap by a few dollars especially on renewals. Namecheap's renewal price is semi-hidden/obscured... considering a switch since it means a hundred or two dollars a year in savings.

I tried finding a reason to use Porkbun over something like namecheap and I couldn't. The porkbun UI is just barebones, it isn't better than anything else. Porkbun's prices are equal to or higher than most registrars.

They've cranked up the fees for renewals [at another registrar]. New registrations of .com domains are €11 whereas renewals are €32... So one by one I'm moving them all to Porkbun. Seems great so far.
I use them for all my domains, albeit with a passkey for my account. My domains are bought 10 years into the future though, so I rarely login.

I have been quite happy with Porkbun. But I also was aware of Proton's CEO and Proton the company's vocal far right endorsements... Now, I am really not sure how to react to this Proton+Porkbun relationship.

I've long been a big fan of Porkbun, switching over to them from namecheap who I supported from back in the SOPA era. But today Im very frustrated. A friend of mine was required to go through Age ID... despite no legal requirement.
That's not selling out. They explain that it's to combat abuse and that this was not their first choice. They are not requiring ID/face scans for the same reason Discord and Roblox are.
Similar to LinkedIn's 'verified' process, Porkbun uses a 3rd party: veriff.com... Porkbun's policy says that this information is deleted as soon as they have verified that you 'pass.'

You have already burned through a pretty high multiple of whatever margin they make from $10 domains so the fact they're pretty civil says a lot about the company and their approach to customer service.
Tell HN: Porkbun charges $50/hr to resolve unauthorized 3rd party access.

I just signed up a customer to Porkbun. During the billing setup. He had to go through an intrusive ID verification scanning his face and drivers license... Porkbun uses Veriff and they say there one of the good guys, but 3rd party policies can change without notice.
